outputs.explanation: Scatter plot where each of the 141 samples is plotted as an individual point; marginal histograms show distributions. Individual data points are the plotted data itself.

Each point represents a mean ± s.d. across 6 (or fewer) replicate samples per reporter/cell line, but only the mean and error bar are shown; the underlying individual replicate measurements are not overlaid.
Continuous density/line plots of fitted normal distributions for subtype-averaged periods and amplitudes; line plots are exempt from requiring individual point overlays.
Box plots showing ridge lengths per cell line have individual sample points (colored dots for Per2-Luc/Bmal1-Luc) overlaid on the boxes.

Polar histograms depict distributions of phase differences (probability-normalized), which is a histogram type similarly exempt from needing individual point overlay, as the bars themselves represent the distribution of underlying observations.
Polar histogram averaged by subtype, same distribution-type plot as (E); histograms are exempt from requiring individual point overlays.
Line plot showing a single example signal trace with a fitted decay curve for illustration; line plots are exempt from requiring individual data point overlays.
Scatter plot where each of the 117 samples is plotted individually (error bars reflect fit parameter uncertainty, not replicate averaging), so individual data points are already shown.
